primary_symptoms.title: What are your main symptoms?
primary_symptoms.subtitle: Select everything that applies. You can change this any time in your profile.

bell_score_baseline.title: How would you describe your typical day?
bell_score_baseline.subtitle: This is the Bell CFS Disability Scale, the scale most ME/CFS clinicians and patients use. Pick whichever description feels closest most days.
bell_score_baseline.100: 100 — No symptoms at rest, no symptoms with exercise, normal overall activity, able to work full-time
bell_score_baseline.90: 90 — No symptoms at rest, mild symptoms with activity, normal overall activity, able to work full-time
bell_score_baseline.80: 80 — Mild symptoms at rest, symptoms worsened by exertion, minimal activity restriction for exertion only
bell_score_baseline.70: 70 — Mild symptoms at rest, some daily activity limitation, functions close to 90% of expected
bell_score_baseline.60: 60 — Mild to moderate symptoms at rest, daily activity limitation, functions 70-90%, can't work full-time in physical jobs
bell_score_baseline.50: 50 — Moderate symptoms at rest, moderate to severe with exercise, overall activity level 70% of expected
bell_score_baseline.40: 40 — Moderate symptoms at rest, moderate to severe with exercise, overall activity level 50-70% of expected
bell_score_baseline.30: 30 — Moderate to severe symptoms at rest, severe with any exercise, overall activity reduced to 50% of expected
bell_score_baseline.20: 20 — Moderate to severe symptoms at rest, unable to do strenuous activity, overall activity 30-50% of expected
bell_score_baseline.10: 10 — Severe symptoms at rest, bedridden most of the time, no travel outside the house
bell_score_baseline.0: 0 — Severe symptoms continuously, bedridden constantly, unable to care for self

pem_onset_delay.title: When do symptoms usually hit after exertion?
pem_onset_delay.subtitle: PEM often doesn't show up right away. Knowing your pattern helps Mya link crashes back to what actually caused them.

tracker.bell_score_hint: Bell CFS Disability Scale — 100 is normal function, 0 is bedridden
tracker.fatigue_score_hint: 0 = none, 10 = as bad as it gets
tracker.pain_score_hint: 0 = none, 10 = as bad as it gets
tracker.woke_rested_hint: Did you feel refreshed when you woke up?
tracker.pem_today_hint: Are you experiencing post-exertional malaise right now?
tracker.pem_today_signpost: This just flags the day. For severity, symptoms, or linking a likely trigger, log it in the Crashes tab.
tracker.temperature_dysregulation: Hot or cold for no reason
tracker.already_logged_subtitle: You can edit today's entry any time.

pace.title: Today's energy envelope
pace.energy_hint: Rate each 0-100. This is Leonard Jason's Energy Envelope method: stay within your available energy to avoid triggering a crash.
pace.budget_hint: Your daily budget. Adjust it if today is a lower-capacity day.
pace.over_budget: Spent is higher than available today
pace.log_exertion_hint: Not required. Useful if you want to flag something specific that might explain a crash later.

dashboard.no_data_yet: Nothing logged yet. Start with today's check-in.

insights.title: Insights
insights.not_enough_data: Log a few more days to get an insight.
insights.dsq_sf_card_body: The DePaul Symptom Questionnaire — Short Form, the validated ME/CFS research instrument.

dsq_sf.title: DSQ-SF Assessment
dsq_sf.subtitle: For each symptom, rate how often it has bothered you over the past 6 months, and how severe it was.
dsq_sf.frequency_legend: 0 = none of the time, 4 = all of the time
dsq_sf.item_next_day_soreness: Next day soreness or fatigue after non-strenuous, everyday activities
dsq_sf.item_minimum_exercise_tired: Minimum exercise makes you physically tired
dsq_sf.item_unrefreshed_on_waking: Feeling unrefreshed after you wake up in the morning
dsq_sf.item_muscle_pain: Pain or aching in your muscles
dsq_sf.item_attention_difficulty: Difficulty paying attention for a long period of time
dsq_sf.item_unsteady_on_feet: Feeling unsteady on your feet, like you might fall
dsq_sf.item_hot_or_cold_for_no_reason: Feeling hot or cold for no reason
dsq_sf.item_sensory_chemical_reaction: Some smells, foods, medications, or chemicals make you feel sick
dsq_sf.attribution: DePaul Symptom Questionnaire — Short Form, developed by Leonard A. Jason, PhD, DePaul University.
